ruling: - **R55. Merge-flow fixes take an express lane.** Owner 13:19 CST Nov 12: "i think in general we heavily prioritize these merge actions (bringing them all express way to main before letting other work get in its way, like even if there's a batch rn looking to go to main it waits". Read: a lane waits a median 536 min, 397 of it before its batch builds (last 15 batch merges). Owner 13:21 CST picked d: "Express lane, and cancel a running batch for it too". 1. A merge-flow lane, once its review passes, goes to main as its own batch, ahead of every other lane. 2. If another batch is in CI then, the batch runner cancels that run first; rule git-no-merge-during-batch-ci still holds, since no run is in progress at the merge. 3. The cancelled batch then merges main in and runs CI again. 4. Merge-flow lanes are the steps of R4, R26, R42 part 2 and R50: lane-lint-once-fail-fast, two-drop-leaves-queue, busy-file-stacked-batches, records-page-before-ready, batch-freeze-lane-set-enforce, merge-flow-after-anthropic and red-job-wakes-runner. Owner 13:45 CST added the auto-build half of merge-batch-split-and-pipeline: "that needs to join the express list". Owner 14:05 CST added CI fixes: "CI fixes need to be right up there in the express lane with the merging fixes given they go hand in hand". That adds the claude-settings CI wall-time steps: mutate-guard-split, convert-time-pinned-tests, timing-tests, page-settle-signals, guard-pr-runs-windows-shards, guard-shard-value-no-slash, rollup-needs-all-shards, and each cut the 14:03 CST CI audit names. A lane outside this list does not take the express lane. Home: decision no-merge-during-batch-ci; skill ci-hygiene step 8 points to it.
